title: Leaving Fats for Stuff Smith and his own group at Philadelphia's Midway
summary: As Fats's work was closing he left, with 'Stormy Weather' being made, and led his own group at the Midway Musical Bar in wartime Philadelphia.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Over the years, were you with Fats's group right to the end of the thing?
Well, yes and no. I'll tell you why I said that, because I had stopped -- I had left Fats to go with well, maybe Stuff Smith. I was with Stuff for a while.
Well, he was only -- on the outs. He was beginning to close, and things were happening, and he didn't look like he was going -- he just made this movie, uh, uh, the last movie he made.

Yeah, 'Stormy Weather', and I had to leave him while he did that, and while he was doing Stormy Weather I was -- had to be working, of course, and things didn't look up and like it was going -- he had a few dates in Boston around, so I then picked up some other guys, side sight guys, you know, let them, picked them up and do it, and they will soon do the thing, and meantime I could see the writing on the --

handwriting on the wall, and I got my own group, and I had a chance to go to Philadelphia, the Midway Musical Bar, so I took a group into there. It's between Market and -- Market Street and what's the name of the street? I don't know. Tch, tch, tch, tch. It's between 15th and 16th Street, and Market and -- Sansom. Sansom Street.

So I was in there with my own group, and it was during the war, and people were happy, and sailors and everybody, and I was making a dollar, and the money was nice. I said aw the heck with it. So he came over the air. He'd gone. I was -- I came home on Monday, you know, my family. And then that's where I heard it.
